verdict.rationale: GitHub documents first-party automation via GitHub Actions for workflows in the repository and CI/CD (github-docs-38, github-docs-11). Headless scripting is supported through the open-source GitHub CLI and the REST/GraphQL APIs with scoped fine-grained tokens (github-docs-31, github-docs-41, github-docs-40, github-docs-19), plus a terminal-based Copilot CLI and an asynchronous cloud agent (github-docs-23, github-docs-26). A community user confirms adopting GitHub's CI/CD; separate complaints about Actions outages and missing org self-hosted runners point to reliability and limitations, not the absence of the capability. Missing for 10: no documented non-interactive or CI mode for Copilot CLI or the agent, the Actions evidence is only one-line marketing descriptions with no runner or headless-auth details, and independent hands-on corroboration of headless automation is limited.
